source.venue: International Journal of Selection and Assessment 10(1-2), 117-125

rows.quote: However, none of the Big Five personality measures were found to be predictors of absenteeism or accidents.
rows.notes: Salgado (2002) meta-analysis found no Big Five trait predicted absenteeism; conscientiousness predicted deviant behaviors and turnover (validity about -.16 for conscientiousness and -.13 for agreeableness with counterproductive behavior per a secondary citation, unverified). Effect is null because no significant value exists; use a near-zero effect. Judge, Martocchio & Thoresen (1997) report extraversion and conscientiousness predicting absence in a small sample, but I could not retrieve the abstract.

source.authors: Brown, S., & Taylor, K.
source.title: Household finances and the 'Big Five' personality traits

rows.quote: For example, a one standard deviation increase in extraversion is associated with a 21.70 percentage point increase in unsecured debt.
rows.notes: UK British Household Panel Survey. The paper's unit for the debt outcome is ambiguous (reads as percent change in the level of debt, not a probability). Couples: one SD of agreeableness is associated with an increase in unsecured debt of over 22 percentage points. Conscientiousness is inversely associated with unsecured debt in every sample. Probability of holding other debt: extraversion +2.44 pp per SD (singles). Greene, Shy & Stavins (2023) separately find that less conscientious, more open, and more agreeable card holders are more likely to revolve credit card debt (no coefficients extracted).

source.authors: Lundberg, S.
source.title: Personality and marital surplus

rows.quote: The effects of individual personality traits on the marriage probabilities of men and women are quite distinct, though there are two common elements in all specifications—openness to experience decreases marriage for both men and women, while conscientiousness increases the probability of marriage.
rows.notes: Value is the average marginal effect of conscientiousness for men from Table 3 column 2 (0.055, SE 0.013), as a probability change (0.055 = 5.5 points) per SD; women 0.031 (SE 0.010). Openness: women -0.044 (SE 0.010), men -0.034 (SE 0.014). Women: extraversion +0.037 (SE 0.013). Traits were standardized by gender (source text). CI is value +/- 1.96 SE. Germany, cohorts born 1945-1970.
